summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatitis C, gastritis, and colonic angioectasias presented with bright red blood in stool and hematemesis after alcohol consumption. He was hemodynamically stable with a hemoglobin of 9.3 g/dL, which slightly decreased to 8.7 g/dL on repeat testing but remained within his baseline chronic anemia range. Evaluation revealed no active bleeding on exam, and possible sources included gastritis exacerbated by alcohol, prior angioectasias, or hemorrhoids. The patient was intoxicated on arrival with a serum ethanol level of 120 mg/dL and positive urine toxicology for opiates and barbiturates. He received IV fluids and proton pump inhibition but insisted on leaving against medical advice after being counseled on the risks. He was discharged home on his prior medications with instructions to follow up for ongoing management of anemia and liver disease.
problems: Unspecified gastritis and gastroduodenitis, without mention of hemorrhage
Acute alcoholic intoxication in alcoholism, unspecified
Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma
Esophageal varices in diseases classified elsewhere, without mention of bleeding
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage I through stage IV, or unspecified
